title: Extremal correlation concentrates weight on level one
statement:
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a $\pm 1$-valued Boolean function that is odd, meaning $f(\lnot x)=-f(x)$ for every $x$, and suppose its Fourier correlation function attains the value
\[
  \mathrm{corr}(f)\;=\;\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\hat f(S)^2\,(-1/3)^{|S|}\;=\;-\tfrac13.
\]
Then $\hat f(S)=0$ for every subset $S\subseteq[n]$ with $|S|\neq 1$; that is, all Fourier--Walsh weight of $f$ is carried by the singleton frequencies.
replaced:
If $\mathrm{corr}(f) = -1/3$, then $\hat f(S) = 0$ for all $S$ with
$|S| \ne 1$.  Combined with oddness ($\hat f(\varnothing) = 0$), all Fourier
weight lies on level 1: $W_1[f] = 1$.
